# Copy mode (toggle_copy_mode, ⌘⇧C): a cursor of its own goes through the
# screen and the scrollback by key, selects and copies; the program gets
# none of the keys.
type:printf '\033[H\033[2J\033[3J'; printf 'alpha beta_gamma\nsecond line here\n\344\270\255\346\226\207 third\n'
key:enter
wait:0.6
key:cmd+shift+c
expect-mode:Copy Mode
key:g
key:g
expect-copy-cursor:alpha beta_gamma@0
key:w
expect-copy-cursor:alpha beta_gamma@6
# Down keeps the column; w to the next word; v, e, y: copied.
key:j
key:w
expect-copy-cursor:second line here@7
key:v
expect-mode:Copy Mode · Visual
key:e
expect-selection:line
key:y
expect-mode:Copied
expect-clipboard:line
expect-copy-cursor:-
expect-selection:-
# Wide characters are one step each.
key:cmd+shift+c
key:g
key:g
key:j
key:j
expect-copy-cursor:中文 third@0
key:l
expect-copy-cursor:中文 third@2
key:l
expect-copy-cursor:中文 third@4
# A click puts the cursor where it is.
click-text:third
expect-copy-cursor:中文 third@5
# ? finds up the page from the cursor; Return comes back to the pane, the
# cursor on the match; Esc leaves copy mode and the search.
key:?
type:beta
expect-searching:1
key:enter
expect-copy-cursor:alpha beta_gamma@6
expect-mode:Copy Mode
key:escape
expect-mode:-
expect-searching:0
# The keys never reached the shell: its command line is as it was.
type:echo DONE-$((40+2))
key:enter
expect:DONE-42
expect-not:command not found
